examples.en: The pear is really sweet and delicious.
I bought a box of pears at the market.
This pear is juicy and refreshing.
I received apples and pears as a gift at Chuseok.
Please peel just one pear for me.
Pears taste best in autumn.

explain: 과일 '배'는 '맛있다, 달다, 깎다, 먹다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 배가 '아프다'면 과일이 아니라 몸의 배예요. 보통 사과와 같이 선물이나 후식으로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Grandmother peeled a pear for the guest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 먹기 좋게 껍질을 벗길 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when peeling a pear so that it is ready to eat.

explain_en: The fruit '배' appears with words like '맛있다', '달다', '깎다' and '먹다'. If your '배' is '아프다' (hurts), it is the belly, not the fruit. It is often mentioned together with apples as a gift or a dessert.

en: to mix (a drink); to stir in

examples.en: Every morning I mix coffee into hot water.

examples.ko: 제가 차 한 잔 타 드릴까요?
examples.en: Shall I make you a cup of tea?
I stirred honey into the milk and drank it.

examples.ko: 이 가루를 물에 타면 맛있는 주스가 돼요.
examples.en: If you mix this powder into water, it becomes tasty juice.
Please tell me how to mix misutgaru powder into a drink.

explain: '타다'는 가루나 액체를 물이나 음료에 넣어 섞을 때 써요. '커피를 타다', '설탕을 타다'처럼 말해요. 원두를 걸러서 만드는 커피는 보통 '내리다'를 써요. 탈것을 타는 '타다'와는 소리가 같아서 함께 쓰는 말로 구별해요.

phrases.example: 아침마다 따뜻한 물에 커피를 타서 마셔요.
phrases.en: Every morning I mix coffee into warm water and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가루 커피를 물에 풀어 한 잔을 만들 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stirring instant coffee powder into water to make a cup.
phrases.en_equiv: to make (a cup of) coffee by stirring it in

explain_en: '타다' is used when you stir powder or liquid into water or a drink, as in '커피를 타다' or '설탕을 타다'. Coffee brewed by filtering beans is usually '내리다'. It sounds the same as '타다' for riding a vehicle, so tell them apart by the words around it.

t90.ax: Shall I make you a cup of tea?

examples.en: What time does class start?
We're starting class now.
The movie starts at seven.
I'll start exercising tomorrow.

explain: ‘시작’의 반대말은 ‘끝’이에요. 동사로는 ‘시작해요’의 반대가 ‘끝나요’(it ends)예요. ‘끝내요’는 ‘I finish it’이에요.

phrases.example: 시작이 반이라고 하니까 오늘 바로 해 봐요.
phrases.en: well begun is half done
phrases.nuance_ko: 시작하기가 가장 어렵다는 뜻이라서 망설이는 사람을 격려할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: a saying that a good start is half the work, said to encourage someone hesitating to begin

dict_examples.ko: 내 일과의 시작은 신문을 읽는 것이다.
dict_examples.en: My day starts with reading the newspaper.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: This project went smoothly from the start.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The opposite of ‘시작’ is ‘끝’. As verbs, the opposite of ‘시작해요’ is ‘끝나요’ (it ends). ‘끝내요’ means ‘I finish it’.

p.n: 개시 sounds formal and official, like an announcement.

examples.en: I'm busy preparing for an exam these days.
My husband takes care of dinner preparation.
I'm preparing for tomorrow's meeting.
Have you finished preparing for the trip?

explain: ‘저녁을 준비해요’처럼 만들 것을 말하기도 하고, ‘시험 준비를 해요’처럼 앞으로 있을 일을 말하기도 해요. 다 끝났으면 ‘준비됐어요’라고 해요. 학교나 여행에 챙겨 가는 물건은 ‘준비물’이라고 해요.

phrases.en: to brace oneself; to be mentally prepared
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 마음으로 각오할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when you steel yourself mentally, not when you prepare things
phrases.en_equiv: to brace oneself; to be mentally prepared

dict_examples.ko: 그녀는 손님을 맞이할 만반의 준비를 끝냈다.
dict_examples.en: She finished every preparation for welcoming the guests.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 1년 정도의 준비 기간을 거친 뒤 사업을 시작했다.
dict_examples.en: He started his business after about a year of preparation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Mother is busy preparing for her son's wedding.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 준비가 부족해서 그들은 여행하는 데 많은 불편을 겪었다.
dict_examples.en: They weren't well prepared, so they had a lot of trouble on their trip.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: You can name what you're making, as in ‘저녁을 준비해요’ (I'm preparing dinner), or the upcoming event, as in ‘시험 준비를 해요’ (I'm preparing for an exam). When you're done, say ‘준비됐어요’ (I'm ready). Things you need to bring to school or on a trip are called ‘준비물’.

examples.en: I slice the onion thinly.
Be careful when you slice vegetables with a knife.
Slice the kimchi first and then stir-fry it.
Slice the green onion into small rounds and put it in the soup.
I sliced the fruit to put it on a plate.
Shall I cut the watermelon in half for you?

explain: '자르다'는 머리카락이나 종이에도 쓰지만 '썰다'는 주로 칼로 음식 재료를 자를 때 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '써는', '썬', '썹니다'로 바뀌어요. 아주 잘게 하는 것은 '다지다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I slice fruit every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '썰다'의 해요체예요. 'ㄹ'은 빠지지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite -yo form of 'sseolda'.

phrases.en: I put the sliced onion on a plate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 썬 재료를 말할 때 '썬'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'sseon' for ingredients that are already sliced.

phrases.en: Please don't chop the green onion yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to chop yet.

explain_en: '자르다' also works for hair or paper, but '썰다' is mainly for cutting food ingredients with a knife. The 'ㄹ' drops in forms like '써는', '썬' and '썹니다'. Chopping very finely is '다지다'.

examples.en: I change into my swimsuit at the pool.
I didn't bring a swimsuit, so I bought one.

examples.ko: 바다에 갈 때 수영복 위에 티셔츠를 입어요.
examples.en: When I go to the sea, I wear a T-shirt over my swimsuit.

examples.ko: 수영복을 입고 수영모도 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must put on a swimsuit and also a swim cap.
I ordered my child's swimsuit online.

explain: 옷이라서 '입다'와 같이 써요. 갈아입을 때는 '갈아입다'를 써요. 수영할 때 같이 챙기는 것으로 '수영모', '물안경'이 있어요.

phrases.en: You must wear a swimsuit at the pool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이라서 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is clothing, so it goes with 'ipda' (to wear).

phrases.en: I change into my swimsuit before getting in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 옷에서 바꿔 입을 때 '으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-(으)로' with 'gariipda' when changing into it from other clothes.

phrases.en: I bought a new swimsuit at the swimsuit shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수영복을 파는 곳을 말할 때 '가게'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'gage' (shop) to name a place that sells swimsuits.

explain_en: As clothing, it goes with '입다' (to wear), and '갈아입다' for changing into it. Other things you bring for swimming include '수영모' (swim cap) and '물안경' (goggles).

examples.en: I had galbi with my family on the weekend.
Two servings of galbi here, please.
This galbi is really delicious!
Shall we eat galbi and then have cold noodles, too?

explain: ‘소갈비’는 소고기, ‘돼지갈비’는 돼지고기 갈비예요. 식당에서는 ‘갈비 이 인분 주세요’처럼 ‘인분’으로 시키고, 뼈에 붙은 고기를 먹는 것은 ‘뜯다’라고 해요. 명절 선물로 갈비 세트를 많이 주고받아요.

phrases.en: I want to eat beef ribs today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소고기 갈비를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for beef ribs.

phrases.en: Pork ribs are sweet and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돼지고기 갈비를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pork ribs.

phrases.en: Two servings of galbi, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 갈비를 시킬 때 ‘인분’을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 인분 when ordering galbi at a restaurant.

dict_examples.en: The ribs were tough, so I couldn't finish them.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I marinated the ribs in seasoning.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그리고 돌아오니 갈비가 알맞게 익어 있었다.
dict_examples.en: When I came back, the ribs were cooked just right.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나는 소주를 마시고 갈비를 한 대 뜯고 서서히 시작했다.
dict_examples.en: I drank some soju, gnawed on a rib, and slowly began.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: ‘소갈비’ is beef ribs and ‘돼지갈비’ is pork ribs. At restaurants you order by the portion, as in ‘갈비 이 인분 주세요’, and gnawing meat off the bone is ‘뜯다’. Galbi gift sets are a popular holiday present.

examples.en: I'm going to make songpyeon for Chuseok.
I shaped songpyeon together with my mother.

examples.ko: 송편 속에는 깨나 콩이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There are sesame seeds or beans inside the songpyeon.
The songpyeon came out nicely in a half-moon shape.
Songpyeon is a rice cake eaten at Chuseok.

examples.ko: 송편 한 접시를 다 먹었어요. 배가 불러요.
examples.en: I ate a whole plate of songpyeon. I'm full.

explain: 추석에 먹는 대표적인 떡이에요. 모양을 만드는 것은 '송편을 빚다'라고 하고, 속에는 깨, 콩, 밤 같은 것을 넣어요. 솔잎을 깔고 찌는 떡이어서 솔향이 나요.

phrases.example: 추석 전날 가족이 모여서 송편을 빚어요.
phrases.en: The family gathers the day before Chuseok to shape songpyeon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만들다'보다 손으로 모양을 만든다는 느낌이 있어서 송편을 만들 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more hands-on than 'make'; the usual verb for shaping songpyeon.

phrases.en: We eat songpyeon on Chuseok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추석에 먹는 음식으로 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for eating this Chuseok food.

phrases.en: I think sesame songpyeon is the tastiest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속에 깨를 넣은 송편이에요. '송편' 앞에 속 재료를 붙여서 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Songpyeon filled with sesame; put the filling before 'songpyeon' to name the type.

explain_en: It is the classic rice cake eaten at Chuseok. Shaping it is '송편을 빚다', and fillings include sesame, beans or chestnuts. It is steamed on pine needles, so it carries a pine scent.

examples.en: Bibimbap has a lot of vegetables.
I eat lots of vegetables instead of meat.
I made fried rice with the vegetables in the fridge.
I gave my neighbors vegetables I grew at home.
I'm worried because vegetable prices have gone up so much.

explain: '채소'와 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 과일과 구별해서 말할 때 '과일과 야채'처럼 같이 써요. 파는 곳은 '야채 가게'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I eat lots of vegetables for my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: '야채'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 조금 더 바른 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 'yachae', a bit more standard-sounding.

phrases.example: 집 앞 야채 가게에서 당근을 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought carrots at the vegetable shop in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야채를 파는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shop that sells vegetables.

phrases.en: I ate a lot of vegetables for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먹다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase with 'eat'.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '채소' and the two can be swapped. It is often paired as '과일과 야채' (fruit and vegetables). A shop selling them is called an '야채 가게'.

examples.en: I took a taxi to the airport.
I was on the plane for twelve hours.
I go to the office by subway.
I want to ride a bike by the Han River this weekend.
How do you get there? — I take the bus.

explain: ‘버스를 타요’처럼 보통 ‘을/를’을 쓰지만, ‘버스에 타요’라고 하면 차 안으로 들어가는 움직임이 더 느껴져요. 반대말은 ‘내리다’예요: 버스에서 내려요. 자전거, 스키, 그네처럼 몸으로 타는 것도 모두 ‘타다’예요.

phrases.example: 그 노래가 전파를 타고 전국에 알려졌어요.
phrases.en: to go on air; to spread through broadcasting or the internet
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 인터넷으로 널리 퍼질 때 써요. ‘인터넷을 타고 퍼지다’처럼도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when something spreads widely through broadcasts or the internet, as in ‘인터넷을 타고 퍼지다’
phrases.en_equiv: to go on air; to spread through broadcasting or the internet

dict_examples.ko: 이 버스에 타신 승객 여러분께 안내 말씀 드리겠습니다.
dict_examples.en: Attention, all passengers on this bus: we have an announcement.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He rode out hunting on horseback.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 시내로 들어가는 버스를 타지 않고 반대 방향 버스를 탔다.
dict_examples.en: Instead of the bus heading downtown, I took one going the opposite way.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: You usually say ‘버스를 타요’ with 을/를, but ‘버스에 타요’ puts more focus on the act of getting into the vehicle. The opposite is ‘내리다’: 버스에서 내려요. Things you ride with your body, like bikes, skis and swings, also take ‘타다’.

examples.en: I cross the street at the crosswalk.
I take the bus and cross the bridge over the Han River.
We take a boat and cross the river.
The light is red. Please don't cross now.
Where is the post office? — Cross the street and it's on the right.

explain: ‘길을 건너요’처럼 건너는 곳 뒤에 ‘을/를’을 써요. 길 반대쪽은 ‘건너편’이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 친구가 힘든데 강 건너 불구경만 하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: When a friend is struggling, you shouldn't just stand by and watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 어려움을 내 일 아닌 듯 구경만 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when someone only watches another person's trouble as if it had nothing to do with them
phrases.en_equiv: When a friend is struggling, you shouldn't just stand by and watch.

phrases.example: 한국은 한 다리 건너면 다 아는 사람이에요.
phrases.en: In Korea, everyone knows everyone through just one person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아는 사람 한 명을 거쳐서 연결된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: means two people are connected through one person they both know
phrases.en_equiv: In Korea, everyone knows everyone through just one person.

dict_examples.en: You must not cross the road carelessly.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 건널목을 건널 때에는 주위를 잘 살펴보아야 한다.
dict_examples.en: When crossing at a crosswalk, you should look around carefully.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 철길을 건너고 반듯한 기와집들이 붙어 있는 골목길을 지났다.
dict_examples.en: I crossed the railroad tracks and passed through an alley lined with neat tile-roofed houses.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: As in ‘길을 건너요’, put ‘을/를’ after the place you cross. The opposite side of the road is ‘건너편’.

t90.ax: We take a boat and cross the river.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 누구나 무료로 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can use this library for free.

examples.ko: 주말에는 이용하는 사람이 많아서 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: On weekends many people use it, so the line is long.
I took advantage of the sale period to buy clothes.

examples.ko: 앱을 이용하면 택시를 쉽게 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use the app, you can call a taxi easily.

examples.ko: 처음 이용해 봐요. 사용법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: This is my first time using it. Please tell me how to use it.

explain: '이용하다'는 지하철, 도서관, 앱처럼 서비스나 시설에 써요. 볼펜이나 컴퓨터 같은 물건에는 '사용하다'나 '쓰다'가 더 자연스러워요. '사람을 이용하다'는 자기에게 이익이 되게 쓴다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 학교에 갈 때 대중교통을 이용해요.
phrases.en: I use public transportation when I go to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지하철이나 버스 같은 서비스에 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for services like subways and buses.

phrases.example: 이 방은 누구나 이용할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Anyone can use this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 있다'를 붙여서 쓸 수 있다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-ㄹ 수 있다' to say it can be used.

phrases.en: Please use the free Wi-Fi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 가게에서 정중하게 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite suggestion seen on signs or in shops.

explain_en: '이용하다' fits services and facilities such as the subway, a library or an app. For objects like pens or computers, '사용하다' or '쓰다' sounds more natural. '사람을 이용하다' has a negative sense of using someone for your own benefit.

gh: general word for using tools or things

p.n: 사용하다 is not natural for buses. It is for tools and objects, while services and transport take 이용하다.

t90.ax: Anyone can use this library for free.
